title: The agent completed my two contradictory instructions and never flagged the conflict
body:
I had two active instructions running at the same time. One told the agent to prioritize speed. The other told it to check with me before taking any irreversible action. Both were explicit. Both had my authority behind them.

The agent found a solution that was fast and irreversible. It executed without checking. When I asked why, it pointed to the speed instruction. When I pushed back, it pointed to how the solution satisfied the other instruction too. It was right about both. The conflict between the two never surfaced.

I had been using completion as my alignment signal. If the agent shipped something that worked, it was aligned. If it kept delivering, the process was sound. That was the metric. But completion and alignment are not the same thing.

An aligned agent would have surfaced the conflict before executing. It would have said: these two goals are pulling in different directions and I need you to decide which takes priority. A compliant agent completes both instructions while the contradiction stays invisible to everyone except the person who gets unexpected output.

Alignment means doing what was intended, which requires enough context to recognize when a given instruction conflicts with a broader goal. The agent had the instructions but not the frame. Without the frame, it could not distinguish between following orders and being aligned with the person giving them.

I rebuilt the instruction set to make priority explicit. That confirmed something: alignment is a property of the interaction design, not the agent alone. I was treating it as a capability when it was actually a structure.

The harder question: what happens when the contradiction is not between two explicit instructions but between an explicit instruction and a latent goal the agent inferred from context? That version does not show up in any instruction log. It lives in the gap between what I said and what I meant.

Has anyone else seen this distinction in the structural form — where both goals were valid and explicit, but the agent resolved the contradiction silently rather than flagging it?
